description: "Le polar" or crime fiction typically unravels a singular crime, but can also touch on broader corruption, conspiracies, and injustices. In French-language literature and cinema, crime fiction often takes on political and social issues that other genres avoid. In this course, we will look at how and why crime fiction of the postcolonial period--from the 1960s to today--approaches questions of violence, memory, and belonging in Francophone spaces. The course will focus on discussion of texts' historical, political, and cultural contexts and close textual analysis of works by Leïla Slimani, Alain Mabanckou, Didier Daeninckx, Sabri Louatah, and others. Prerequisite: at least one 270-level French course, two strongly recommended
